app.title: RaceForge
start.live: Connect to the real car: status, latency, drive by hand (teleop), STOP.
live.race_mode: Race mode: the car refuses teleop and live commands.
live.pair_phone_hint: In TrackScout tap the steering wheel → ⋯ → Pair car → Scan QR code. The phone then drives the car directly over Wi-Fi; the code contains the token, so only show it to your team.
teleop.title: Teleop
teleop.help: Xbox: hold RB to drive, RT/LT forward/reverse, left stick steers, B = stop. Keyboard: W/S or ↑/↓, A/D or ←/→, Space = stop. Touch: drag the joystick. Letting go stops the car.
start.scans: Look at corridor scans from TrackScout: mesh, camera path, passes.
scans.none: No scans yet. Record with TrackScout and upload, or open a .tscan file.
scans.pick: Pick one or more passes on the left.
engine.ldraw_missing: LDraw library missing — run `raceforge parts fetch` for real LEGO geometry
start.intro: Build a car, drive it in a generated corridor and replay the runs.
start.parts: Browse the LEGO and device catalogue
start.construct: Configure a quick-start car and see it in 3D
start.simulate: Run a controller in a corridor with opponents
construct.save_login: Log in on the Team tab and pick a workspace to save versions.
team.register_hint: Uses the server address, username and password from the form above.
team.invite_hint: Send this link to the teammate; it works once and expires after 7 days.
team.token_once: Copy it now — it is shown only once.
team.saved_offline: Saved locally — it syncs when the backend is reachable
team.conflicts: {{count}} conflicts: versions made in parallel from the same parent are kept as branches
team.no_objects: Nothing saved in this workspace yet.
team.totp_why: Required for admins, recommended for everyone: the backend is reachable from the internet.
team.totp_secret: Add this key to an authenticator app (e.g. Google Authenticator, 2FAS), then enter the 6-digit code:
team.trackscout_hint: In TrackScout open Settings → Scan QR code. The code contains a new token (read + edit only) for this workspace and this laptop's key; revoke it below under API tokens if a phone is lost.
team.trackscout_loopback: The phone cannot reach this server address (it only works on this computer). For a test in your Wi-Fi start the backend with “raceforge backend dev --lan”, log in with the address it prints, then pair again.
team.trackscout_slow: Backend connection slow: {{rate}} MB/s, about {{minutes}} min
team.trackscout_when_faster: Upload when the connection is faster
deploy.title: Deploy to the car
deploy.usb_written: Written to {{path}}. Eject the stick, plug it into the car's board, then check the result.
deploy.usb_pending: No result yet: plug the stick into the car's board first.
start.train: Benchmark controllers on held-out corridors and tune their parameters automatically (Optuna).
train.overfit: Worse than the defaults on the held-out corridors (overfitting): use more trials or training corridors.
train.written: Parameters written to {{path}} — use them in Deploy (Parameters).
train.help: Score = mean time to finish; a car that does not finish counts as time limit plus the share of the race it missed.
start.tracks: Draw a corridor (e.g. your school hallway) in 2D and race on it in the simulator.
tracks.name: Name
tracks.help: Click to add centreline points in driving order, drag to move, right-click to delete. Obstacles: pick a type, then click. The walls are built automatically at the chosen width.
tracks.saved_ok: Saved — pick it in Simulate under Track.
tracks.measured: Tape measure (m) for the next check
tracks.check_line: Check {{n}}: model {{model}} m, tape {{measured}} m ({{err}} cm)
tracks.width_measured: Scan width along the line: median {{median}} m, narrowest {{min}} m ({{n}} samples)
tracks.width_none: No closed corridor along the line in the scan
tracks.scan_walls_help: Walls follow the scanned corridor and the line moves to its middle. Gaps in the scan continue the neighbouring wall; the corridor width is only used for a side without any wall.
train.runs: Runs (different sensor noise and object placement)
editor.open_hint: Opens this car in the parts editor (move, turn, add, delete, snap). Changing the quick-start fields afterwards starts a new car.
editor.pick: Click a part to select it.
editor.linked: This part is in a linked submodel: the change applies to every copy.
editor.help: Arrows / PageUp / PageDown move one stud (Shift: 1 LDU). R / T / Y turn 90° about z / x / y (Shift: back). Delete removes. Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo / redo. Shift+click selects several. Ctrl+D duplicates, M makes a mirror copy (left ↔ right). Esc deselects.
rules.title: Rules
rules.stale: Price older than 30 days — check it again
rules.price_hint: LEGO parts from the school kit cost 0 € unless you enter a price. Prices are saved on this computer.
rules.limits: Limits from the race rules (empty = not set)
rules.wheels_steering_lego_ok: Wheels and steering mechanism are LEGO
rules.wheels_steering_lego_fail: Wheels and steering mechanism must be LEGO (click to show)
rules.steering_submodel_lego_ok: Steering submodel is LEGO only (motor exempt)
rules.steering_submodel_lego_fail: Non-LEGO part in the steering submodel (only the steering motor may be non-LEGO)
rules.ev3_drives_ok: The EV3 has a driving function
rules.ev3_drives_fail: The EV3 must drive at least one function (EV3 brick + EV3 motor)
editor.add_docks: Click a part: it docks onto the selected part (Tab: next position).
editor.add_free: Click a part to add it (select a part first to dock onto it).
parts.unverified: added by the team — mass and connectors unverified
parts.holes_hint: Beams/liftarms: number of pin holes in a row (creates the connectors)
parts.length_hint: Pins/axles: length in studs (creates the end connectors)
parts.added: {{name}} is in the catalogue now (also in the editor).
parts.printed_summary: {{size}} mm · {{volume}} cm³ · about {{mass}} g · print cost about {{cost}} €
parts.not_watertight: Mesh is not closed: volume from the convex hull (too high).
train.params_saved: Saved to {{path}} — use it in Deploy.
train.worker_help: Make a computer a worker: log in on the Team tab, then run `raceforge worker register` and `raceforge worker run` (add --idle-only to use it only when it is not busy).
parts.new_connector: Click on the part adds a
parts.connectors_help: The axis points along the surface normal (flip it if needed). Pins/axles go into holes along this axis.
parts.connectors_saved: {{count}} connectors saved — the part now snaps and docks in the editor.
train.rl_help: Learns a driving policy in the simulator (needs the 'rl' extra: uv sync --extra rl). 200 000 steps take roughly 15–60 min; long runs belong on a team worker.
train.policy_written: Policy saved to {{path}} — deploy controllers/templates/onnx_policy.py with this file as parameters.
worker.title: This computer as a team worker
worker.enable: Run team jobs on this computer
worker.mode_idle: only when nobody uses it (and on mains power)
worker.reason_idle_unknown: idle time unknown here — use 'always' or 'at fixed times'
worker.help: A running job is paused after the current race when you use the computer again; another worker continues it.
train.all_states: Use every frame (also controller drives), not only teleop
train.bc_help: Record demonstrations first: Simulate → controller "none – drive by hand", tick "Record run", drive several clean laps with gamepad/keyboard. Real-car logs work too. Needs the 'rl' extra.
train.no_recordings: No recordings yet — record a teleop drive in Simulate first.
live.share: Share with the team (live view + run log)
live.share_offline: Team backend not reachable — the drive is still recorded
live.team_none: No teammate is sharing a car right now.
tracks.localise_hint: Map + racing line as params for controllers/templates/localised.py (save the track first)
tracks.localise_path: Where should the params YAML go?
tracks.localised: Saved {{path}} — deploy it with the localised controller.
deploy.test_info: Test bundle: live view, teleop and the test speed limit work; radios may be on.
deploy.race_info: Race bundle: the car arms only when every radio is off; no live view, no teleop, no test speed limit. Emergency stop stays active.
deploy.race_confirm:
Build a RACE bundle?

• The car only starts when Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and radio dongles are off.
• No live view, no teleop, no remote stop.
• The test speed limit is lifted (car maximum).

The hardware emergency stop stays active.
race.title: Race-day checklist
race.item_radios: Radio pre-check passes (race mode would arm)
race.item_race_bundle: Installed bundle is a race bundle
race.item_spare_car: Spare car ready with the same bundle
race.item_calibration: Calibration done on the race corridor
race.saved: Saved as a note in the car log.
race.radio_unsupported: This car runtime cannot run the pre-check yet — update it.
race.not_race_bundle: The installed bundle is a test bundle: build and install a race bundle for the race.
race.hint: The radio pre-check runs the same check as arming race mode, without arming. Remove radio dongles before the race.
rc.title: Race Control
rc.saved: Saved as run {{run}} in the team workspace.
rc.hint: Show this on a laptop/beamer/iPad facing the start grid: five red lights, then lights out = GO. Tap a car's LAP button each time it crosses the finish line.
calib.title: Calibration (this car)
calib.straight_help: 1. Mark 2 m on the floor. Record, drive straight with teleop (steering 0) over the mark, stop, enter the measured distance, evaluate.
calib.circle_help: 2. Record a few full-lock circles to the left, then to the right (teleop), evaluate.
calib.applied: Saved in {{car}}'s config (previous version: .bak). Build and deploy a new bundle.
